name: Tokyo
limitations: All 31 subpillars are reviewed, not all are measured. Scores require the stated assumptions; unknown evidence remains unknown. This is neither a global ranking nor an exclusion bound. Rejecting a necessary assumption requires reassessment, not automatic retention of its score.

dimensions.rationale: Residential seismic estimates, implemented cooling facilities and public heat information, alongside disaster medical preparation, support protection; heat burden, wooden-housing gaps and unreviewed hazards and locations remain material.
dimensions.assumption: Observed protection usually works and other major hazards do not already cause broader unmitigated failure; rejecting this assumption leaves PCS unresolved.

dimensions.rationale: The 2025 civil-protection revision addresses missile response, but historical events and a plan do not establish current local impact or mitigation effectiveness.
dimensions.assumption: Current organised violence, regional conflict and strategic mitigation have not been sufficiently cross-checked for an overall judgment; unknown is not unsafe.

dimensions.rationale: Delivered medical-service changes, public information, resident surveys and an actual exercise debrief support execution; group reach and real crisis recovery remain incomplete.
dimensions.assumption: Observed execution persists and supports usual operation of major services; surveys and exercises do not measure whole-FUA institutional outcomes.

dimensions.rationale: Actual water operations, regional electricity continuity and monthly Tokyo produce-market deliveries support ordinary resource supply; partial blackout backup, shared power/fuel dependencies and household spending constraints prevent a high-grade judgment.
dimensions.assumption: Observed ordinary supply persists across the functional area and necessary food, water and energy are usually obtainable and affordable for the median-income local resident; operator areas, wholesale flows and household means do not measure that full profile. Rejecting this assumption leaves RES unresolved.

dimensions.rationale: Actual emergency and specialist care, referral pathways and specified insurance cost protection support access; ambulance pressure, dialysis coordination gaps, routine quality and waits remain constraints or unknowns.
dimensions.assumption: Necessary care is usually obtainable, clinically adequate and affordable under usual coverage, and observed delivery persists; national caps do not measure median local household burdens.

dimensions.rationale: A credible early-Alzheimer clinical result, regulator conditions and actual local annual drug-administration cases establish a limited translation pathway; eligibility, safety, cost and broad access remain restricted.
dimensions.assumption: The reviewed disease-specific pathway supports limited health-longevity translation readiness and delivery persists; rejecting representativeness or access leaves LON unresolved, not automatically 40.

dimensions.rationale: Actual annual research and collaborations, network samples and digital-use surveys support research, industry connections and partial diffusion; whole-FUA output, multiple industries and independent critical nodes remain unverified.
dimensions.assumption: Observed research, industry connections and digital capabilities persist; survey denominators and selection do not establish random-sample reach among median-income local citizens.

dimensions.rationale: Airport directories, conditional overseas pension payments and youth mobility programmes support limited leads, not ordinary residents' complete exit capabilities.
dimensions.assumption: Actual independent transport, ordinary-age long-term eligibility, funds and communication continuity remain unresolved; directory points, youth rights and pensions do not fill them.
